item.title: Will Cunningham Leads Legacy Ranch Past Sam Houston, 49-19
item.description: Sam Houston junior Aidan Ward prays before the Class 5A Division II first-round playoff game between Sam Houston and Legacy Ranch at Alamo Stadium on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, in San Antonio, Texas. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) In Legacy Ranch's inaugural varsity season, the Wranglers have notched their first playoff victory, in large part because of quarterback Will Cunningham. The junior had his way with Sam Houston's defense in the opening round of the Class 5A Division II playoffs, tossing for 250 yards and four touchdowns in a 49-19 romp of the Hurricanes on Friday at Alamo Stadium. "He's done it all year, man," Legacy Ranch coach Tim Knicky said. "He's the leader of this football team. The team follows him. We've got a chance as long as we've got Will Cunningham back there." Cunningham completed 4-of-4 passes on the Wranglers' opening drive, putting junior Troy Ramos in position to punch in a 4-yard touchdown. Legacy Ranch converted a 2-point try to take an early 8-0 lead. On its first drive, the Hurricanes drove to the Wranglers' 1-yard line, but back-to-back penalties pushed them back to the 13, where they turned the ball over on downs. Then, from his own 18-yard line, Cunningham hit junior Landon Jordan for a 36-yard gain. Cunningham hit Jordan in stride again on the next play for a 46-yard touchdown. This time, though, the Wildcat's 2-point try was no good. For Sam Houston, the game got worse before it got better as a botched punt set Legacy Ranch up at the Hurricanes' 12-yard line. Cunningham hit junior Ritvik Kasireddy for an 11-yard score that put Legacy Ranch up 21-0 with :03 left in the first quarter. Sam Houston junior Mario Ringo provided a spark on the Hurricanes' ensuing kickoff with a large return. After a sack and an incompletion, junior Xavier Youngblood connected totaled 39 yards through the air and on the ground to get Sam Houston inside the Wranglers' 5-yard line. Junior Jaidon Hamilton spun his way in for the 3-yard score, putting the Hurricanes on the board. Sam Houston's 2-point try was unsuccessful. Now with some momentum, the Hurricanes forced their first punt of the game. Their next drive stalled, though. It was still early in the game, but coach Rashard Colquitt and Sam Houston were in desperation mode. On fourth-and-10, Colquitt called for a fake punt. Senior Miveon Ross took the direct snap and picked up the first down. The Hurricanes' drive continued, and Hamilton scored his second touchdown of the game from 5 yards out. item.description: Argentina v Uruguay - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez has pledged that Argentina will continue working hard under head coach Lionel Scaloni despite suffering a 2-1 friendly loss against Uruguay on Friday. Contesting their first fixture since iconic captain Lionel Messi hung up his international boots last month, the hosts fell short against Diego Forlan's visitors at La Bombonera. Striker scores in Buenos Aires Alvarez found the back of the net in the second half in Buenos Aires, yet his strike proved insufficient to prevent the 2026 World Cup runners-up from losing in front of a sparse home crowd. Following the 39-year-old Messi's emotional farewell victory over Benin last month after 126 goals across 208 caps, the Albiceleste struggled to break down a well-organised visiting defence. Ultimately, Uruguay held firm to hand new manager Forlan his third triumph in charge . Forward welcomes coaching staff continuity Despite the disappointing result, the squad entered the November international window boosted by the news that Scaloni and his backroom team had signed a contract extension to stay in charge of the national side as a new generation takes over from the veterans who defined a trophy-laden era. Speaking to broadcasters after the final whistle about emulating the standards set by the team's departed icons, Alvarez said: "We're going to keep working. We learned and grew during these years with people who gave everything to the National Team; we try to copy that and lead by example." Addressing the dressing room's reaction to the manager extending his tenure, the forward added: "Scaloni told us they were staying on, and that gives us confidence and joy." item.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake edges Troy in final seconds for epic Class A football title win
item.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Troy for the Section 2, Class A title on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Colonie High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - The waning stages of the fourth quarter Friday night for the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team were looking painfully dire, as the Spartans found themselves down a point against Troy and forced to give the ball back on a punt. In a span of a few minutes, BH-BL senior standout Login Tomlinson made two of the biggest plays of his career - the first with his hand and the second with his foot - to flip things back in favor of his team in the Section 2 Class A Super Bowl. First, Tomlinson forced Troy junior quarterback Kyair Carr to fumble the ball away at the Flying Horses' 23-yard line. Then, BH-BL had just 17 seconds left when it had Tomlinson line up for a 32-yard field goal on third down and without a timeout remaining. The senior - following a timeout by Troy - drilled a go-ahead, line-drive boot down the middle in what ended up being a thrilling 23-21 Super Bowl victory over the Flying Horses at Colonie High School. "I have been dreaming about this since I was a little kid and first starting kicking," said Tomlinson, a four-year varsity player who is headed to Siena University to play lacrosse. "It happened. It came true." "It was really nerve-racking out there," BH-BL junior quarterback Tristan West said. "I believed in him every moment when he went out there to kick." The pulse-pounding triumph secured BH-BL (11-0) the program's 11th Class A sectional title in 20 years, and first since 2021. It also marked the first championship guided by fourth-year coach Kevin DeBonis. The loss denied Troy, playing in its second straight Super Bowl, a 10th title since first winning one in 1993. "This feels amazing. Since we were little kids, this is what we have been working for," West said. Last year, the Flying Horses lost to Niskayuna. Troy senior fullback/defensive Ben Mergil, who produced two touchdown receptions and recovered a fumble by BH-BL, emerged from an emotional postgame gathering to put the defeat into context. "It is hard, but, at the end of the day, it is football," Mergil said. "Anybody that has ever played football knows it will teach life lessons. Sometimes, things just don't shake out for you, but you just have to roll with the punches. I want to thank my coaches, my teammates and God for giving me this opportunity to play for such an amazing school and play my heart out." Both squads left everything they had on the field. item.title: UTSA athletics inducts fourth Hall of Fame class
item.description: From left to right, Jessica Rogers, Ryanne Dupree, Teresa Neighbors, Leonard Byrd, and Tamara Luckeymeyer were inducted as the fourth class in the UTSA Athletics Hall of Fame during a ceremony on Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch in Helotes. (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) UTSA inducted three of the San Antonio area's brightest athletics stars into its 2026 Hall of Fame class during a ceremony Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch. East Central's Ryanne DuPree, Judson's Teresa Neighbors and Marshall's Leonard Byrd joined volleyball standout Tamara Luckeymeyer and softball star Jessica Rogers in UTSA's fourth Hall of Fame class. The three track and field standouts from this year's group join a list of UTSA Hall of Fame track athletes that includes Tameka Roberts-Nunez in the inaugural class as well as Starlite Williams and Teddy Williams in 2024. DuPree was a four-time All-American in the multi-events from 2004 to 2007, finishing as high as fourth in the nation and winning nine conference championships. She also holds four UTSA records, including a mark of 13.23 seconds in the 100-meter hurdles. Neighbors' third-place finish as a senior at the 1990 national championships with a mark of 6.74 seconds in the 55-meter run is tied for the highest women's NCAA Indoor individual finish in program history, setting a UTSA record that still stands. She also set then-school records in the 100 and 2000 in 1989, earning another All-America nod. Byrd was a three-time All-American in the 400-meter sprint during his time at UTSA from 1994 to 1997, finishing as high as third in the 1996 outdoor championships. He won four consecutive Southland outdoor conference titles in the event, claiming eight conference championships overall. Luckemeyer won Southland Conference Player of the Year twice in a career that spanned 1997 to 2000, helping the Roadrunners to a regular-season title in 1999 and a tournament championship in 2000. She holds the school records for kills in a career (2,034) and season (567 in 1999). Rogers was a first-team All-Southland selection in each of her four seasons from 2003 to 2007, winning the league's Player of the Year and Hitter of the Year honors in 2005. She stands as the school's career record holder for runs (159), hits (281), extra-base hits (104) and at-bats (732), and in 2005 she led the nation with 0.38 home runs per game. UTSA's Hall of Fame selection committee is made up of designees from the UTSA Alumni Association Board, Letterwinners Club, Roadrunner Foundation and Student-Athlete Advisory Committee, as well as representatives from the university and athletics department along with local print and electronic media. item.title: UCLA endures injury scare, gets heroic return to stay unbeaten
item.description: Ty Dieffenbach #14 of the UCLA Bruins passes the ball against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena, California, Nov. 13, 2026. After taking a shot in the arm, Ty Dieffenbach delivered one. Roars accompanied the UCLA quarterback with each step he took as he jogged back from the locker room to the Rose Bowl sideline late in the third quarter Friday night. It was a heroic return for the veteran who had departed UCLA’s game against Illinois just before halftime with an upper-body injury. The crowd serenaded Dieffenbach with cheers anew once he came onto the field with his team holding a suddenly precarious lead over Illinois. Scooter Jackson (1) of the UCLA Bruins runs for a first down against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena, Calif., Nov. 13, 2026. Getty Images All Dieffenbach did upon his return was to complete each of his five passes on the next drive, including a beautiful touchdown toss, to help the fourth-ranked Bruins hold on for a 22-14 victory that kept their unbeaten record intact. The Bruins could exhale only after an Illinois pass fell incomplete over the middle with 43 seconds left. UCLA had registered another big defensive play only minutes earlier when safety Scooter Jackson came up with an interception – his second of the game – and returned it 41 yards to the Illinois 19-yard line with 2 minutes 42 seconds left. A short Mateen Bhaghani field goal gave the Bruins a 22-14 lead, necessitating a desperation drive by the Fighting Illini that came up well short. Ty Dieffenbach #14 of the UCLA Bruins passes the ball against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena, California, Nov. 13, 2026. Getty Images There were feel-good vibes all around after Dieffenbach escaped injury and UCLA improved to 10-0 for the first time since 1998 – the last season it won a conference championship. The Bruins, who are 7-0 in Big Ten games, need only one more victory in their final two regular-season games – against Michigan and USC – to clinch an appearance in the conference title game. What appeared to be the largest crowd of the season also celebrated a defense that intercepted three passes, registered a sack and recorded six tackles for loss while holding the Fighting Illini (6-4, 4-3) to 240 yards of offense. item.description: Gail Miller, owner of the Utah Royals, is pictured in her office that overlooks America First Field in Sandy on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. | Laura Seitz, Deseret News Gail Miller never thought she’d own a professional women’s sports team again. Over two decades after she and her husband’s WNBA team, the Utah Starzz, moved to San Antonio, Miller reentered the world of women’s sports when The Larry H. Miller Company purchased the NWSL’s Utah Royals FC, along with MLS’s Real Salt Lake, in April 2025. A year later, Miller’s Royals play the Washington Spirit in the semifinals of the NWSL playoffs on Saturday — just two wins shy of the team’s first NWSL championship. Miller was there for the No. 7 Royals’ upset of No. 2 San Diego Wave FC in the quarterfinals. “Oh, it was electric,” she told the Deseret News. “It was so fun to be in an opposing stadium with a win, and especially after how well they played. That’s a big field to defend, and then to be aggressive too, it really showed their talent. It was fun to be there.” On the eve of the Royals’ semifinal match, the Deseret News sat down with Miller at The Larry H. Miller Company office in Sandy, Utah. With a view of America First Field behind her, Miller talked about her love for the Royals, what the club brings to Utah and what it’s like to be the female owner of a professional women’s sports team. Utah Royals owner Gail Miller and her husband, Kim Wilson, high-fives Utah Royals forward Kiana Palacios, who scored the winning goal, at Snapdragon Stadium in San Diego before the Royals' quarterfinal win. | Ava Nash Lead with love There’s a Gail Miller saying that has permeated the Larry H. Miller Company. Miller Sports + Entertainment President Michelle Smith and Utah Royals players quote it in interviews: “Lead with love and success will follow.” Royals players have been vocal throughout the season about the club’s togetherness. item.description: A Bruins trade pitch lands Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin in a proposed package deal centered on Casey Mittelstadt. Getty Casey Mittelstadt of the Boston Bruins. Getty Matthew Poitras of the Boston Bruins would head to Detroit under a new trade pitch. Getty The Boston Bruins came crashing back to Earth Thursday with a humbling 5-2 loss to their archrival Montreal Canadiens at TD Garden. Casey Mittelstadt scored the only two Bruins goals in the lopsided defeat, but under a new trade pitch published Friday and aimed at the Bruins, Boston would trade away its 10-year veteran center and land a three-time All-Star, albeit a disgruntled one in return. The proposed trade would send suspended Red Wings center Dylan Larkin to Boston for Mittelstadt, Matthew Poitras and two 2027 first-round picks. The trade pitch created using the PuckGM simulator tests whether the Detroit Red Wings can end a standoff that has cost Larkin about $41,000 each day since his suspension. Larkin, 30, is a Waterford, Michigan, native whom Detroit selected 15th overall in 2014 after he earned Big Ten Freshman of the Year honors at Michigan. He has played all 12 NHL seasons in Detroit, totaling 278 goals and 649 points in 818 games, including five consecutive 30-goal seasons since 2021-22 . He also won Olympic gold with Team USA in February . Detroit stripped his captaincy on Sept. 11 and suspended him without pay Oct. 29 , after he said he would no longer play for the team. His $8.7 million cap hit runs through 2030-31 , and his no-trade clause gives him control over where he goes. Boston is not on his 10-team list, but the Bruins “would like to get on to Larkin’s list,” TSN’s Darren Dreger said earlier this month , as quoted by Boston.com . How Dylan Larkin Fits the Boston Bruins’ First Line Getty Casey Mittelstadt of the Boston Bruins. Boston’s top line currently features J.J. Peterka, Pavel Zacha and David Pastrnak . Larkin would center Peterka and Pastrnak, pushing Zacha down the lineup, while Mittelstadt and fourth-line center Poitras would be shipped to Detroit. Boston.com ‘s analysis called Larkin an upgrade rather than a franchise-altering player, and it listed Fraser Minten and James Hagens as young centers the Bruins are reluctant to trade, so neither is part of this package. Financially, Boston adds $2.1 million in cap commitments, because Larkin’s $8.7 million replaces Mittelstadt’s $5.75 million and Poitras’s $850,000. Larkin’s remaining salary totals about $38.6 million against $43.5 million in cap charges, so the cash Boston would pay runs roughly $4.9 million below the cap figure. item.title: Naugatuck football rallies past Torrington as Qwentarvous Lee delivers two huge plays
item.description: Naugatuck's Qwentarvous Lee rushed for 133 yards, while scoring on a 78-yard fumble return and an 80-yard run in a 29-14 win over Torrington on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Torrington High. (Steve Barlow/For Hearst Connecticut Media) TORRINGTON - With the annual Thanksgiving battle with Ansonia within sniffing distance, Naugatuck football coach Chris Anderson preached to his team all week long that the Greyhounds couldn't look past Torrington on Friday night. He was right. Naugy found itself trailing by a touchdown at the Robert Frost Athletic Complex, and the gap could have been even greater after another score was called back because of a false start by the Raiders. "At halftime, we told the kids, ‘Well, you've dug yourself a hole, but you've been resilient all season.' We were down to Holy Cross and Woodland, too, and won those games. We can do it again," Anderson remarked following a 29-14 victory that improved the Greyhounds to 9-0. Torrington (6-3) controlled the first half with its ball-control single-wing offense. The Raiders ran 39 plays from scrimmage, more than twice as many as Naugatuck's 17, and ate up big chunks of the clock. Torrington even held the Greyhounds scoreless in the first half for the first time all season. "Yes, we're high-powered, but when you don't have the ball, it doesn't matter," Anderson said. "When you're able to eat the clock like they can, they have the formula to beat us." Naugy, which beat Torrington on the final play each of the past two meetings, needed a big play to turn the tide. Qwentarvous Lee provided exactly that and then did it again. Ahead 8-0 after the opening half, Torrington was driving again on its first possession after intermission. But fullback Cameron Roxbury fumbled at the 22. The ball spun out of the pile to Lee, who picked it up and raced 78 yards to a touchdown. Brandon Andoh's conversion run tied the game for Naugy. "Coach put me in on defense in the second half. I noticed we weren't getting to the ball. I was driving to the ball, and all the effort paid off. The ball came out right in front of me. Josiah (Loyd) stripped it out. The ball came right to me and I took off," Lee said. Nick Coleman got the momentum right back for Torrington with a 61-yard scoring run for his second TD, but Lee immediately answered. On Naugy's next play, he burst through the line and bolted 80 yards for a touchdown. Gabriel Bello's point-after kick put his team ahead for good. "I got Llir (Mamudov) and (Logan) Washenko, two 300-pound guys, in front of me. I told them if you make your blocks and Josiah goes through and blocks the linebacker, I'm going to take off, and that's what happened," Lee said. Torrington answered by driving to the Naugy 6-yard line, but Coleman was stopped short on fourth down. "We just have to keep swarming to the ball. That was the big emphasis for the game," Loyd said. "It means a lot to get to 9-0, especially against a good team like this. They're coached well and have good athletes."

item.description: The Carolina Hurricanes could be dealing with a much larger roster issue given the current run on injuries. It is the first real chance for GMs to meet and discuss trade possibilities with other teams, as well as hold initial meetings with free agents. It was also awards week for MLB, with the yearly awards all announced. Here’s what took place this week. There wasn’t much for free agent deals, but a few were signed this week to kick off free agency. The big news for the Brewers was Jake Bauers signing with the Red Sox , which also means that he turned down the qualifying offer from Milwaukee. Early trade rumors are coming up for current Brewers’ players, mainly focused around the players who are free agents after the 2027 season. item.description: Canada embrace Concacaf experience in win over Guatemala By Ben Steiner A fireworks-filled anthem, a less-than-ideal playing surface, and cages surrounding the pitch. Away days in Concacaf aren’t for the faint of heart, but Canada scraped out a 3-2 win over Guatemala on Friday. Under head coach Jesse Marsch, Canada have faced some of the world's best teams and reached the FIFA World Cup Round of 16. Yet Friday's opening 45 minutes of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals may have been among their most complete, before a disheartening second half saw a 3-0 lead nearly disappear. Jonathan David brought his stellar LaLiga form to the Estadio El Trébol, posting 1g/1a and helping build up Canada’s third goal. Liam Millar, in dominant form in the EFL Championship, scored too, while former Minnesota United striker Tani Oluwaseyi netted his first for Canada in 18 appearances. “We were very happy with that start,” assistant coach Mauro Biello told reporters, taking media duties after Marsch’s second-half red card. “It was something that we addressed here in the build-up to be able to create more, to score more goals, and I think we're very happy with the way our forwards played. Especially in the first half, and getting goals from both strikers and Liam, who was also doing really well at his club.” Alphonso Davies blow It had been more than 600 days since Alphonso Davies last started for Canada, when he tore his ACL in the 2025 Nations League third-place game against the United States . It seemed as if his return, committing to playing for Les Rouges on a November night in Guatemala amid stellar FC Bayern Munich form, was him putting the last two years of injury troubles behind him. That hope lasted just five minutes before an awkward shot block sent him off the pitch early. As of Friday, it was unclear if Davies would be available for the pivotal second leg in Canada or fly back to Germany to recover. His team’s first-half response, though, spoke volumes about the development beyond the 26-year-old’s contributions. “We were all so excited to see Phonzie back, and for him to go down that early, we were just gutted for him,” Oluwaseyi said. “We still played a really good game, and we got a win in a really tough place. A sharp retrieval along the boards by Brock Boeser gave the long-tenured Canuck his 500th-career NHL point , as he recorded the second assist on Pettersson’s goal. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Plain and simple, the New York Rangers took care of business Friday night in Vancouver, overwhelming the last-place Canucks 5-1 at Rogers Arena. Which is exactly what should have been expected. Make no mistake, this is a game the Rangers (12-8-1) had to have. Not only to ensure a winning road trip in the Pacific Northwest, but because the Canucks (3-17-1) are an absolute train wreck, the worst team by far in the NHL. Though the Rangers started slowly in the first period, there was only one expected and acceptable outcome. And that was a Rangers victory. No excuses. Yes, the Canucks are that bad. They’ve now lost seven in a row, and have just one victory in their past 18 games (1-16-1) since Oct. 4 after winning two of their first three. They’re the worst defensive team in the League , allowing more than four and a half goals per game on average, and their penalty kill is simply atrocious. So, even though the Canucks took a 1-0 on an Elias Pettersson deflection at 12:13 of the first period, and the Rangers hadn’t won a game this season after giving up the first goal, there was no way visitors could lose this game. And they didn’t. Gabe Perreault ‘s short-side snipe at 18:47 of the first tied things up. And then it was a master class by the Rangers in the second period. They scored four unanswered goals in a span of 7:49, out-shot the Canucks 12-4, and had a whopping expected goal share 5v5 of 84.02 percent, per Natural Stat Trick . Through two periods, the Rangers had a 16-6 advantage in high-danger chances. They took their foot off the gas some in the third period, but Dylan Garand stopped all 13 shots he faced in the final frame. New York was the far better team at even strength, and on special teams — where they scored once on teh power play and were a perfect 3-for=3 on the penalty kill. Though none of this should come as a surprise. The Rangers took three of four on this road trip, after beginning it with just one road victory on the season. And this latest victory represented their first in nine games when allowing the first goal (1-7-1).4 They reach the season’s quarter-mark third in the Metropolitan Division, and winners in five of their past six games. And without a bitter taste in their collective mouth if they hadn’t taken care of business in a can’t-lose game in Vancouver.
